reading.body:
Hillary Scholten's AI record is mostly data center and energy legislation, not AI safety or model regulation.

Of the 23 events, 14 are bills she sponsored or cosponsored. The largest cluster concerns physical AI infrastructure: the Responsible Data Center Siting Act, the Data Center Resource Disclosure Act, the Defending Our Energy and Water Act, the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act, and the Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act. A second cluster addresses small business AI adoption, and a third covers disclosure and evaluation, including the AI Advertising Disclosure Act and the READ AI Models Act. One bill, H.R. 10519, would create a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program at CISA.

This is the compute and power layer of AI policy rather than the model layer. Siting, resource disclosure, energy and water use, and measurement standards are the questions that arise when data centers are built in a district, and they are the questions a member with data center constituents has reason to legislate on. The record is consistent with a member working the permitting and utility side of AI growth.

The money is small and narrow. Four contributions of $1,000 each appear, three from the Amazon PAC and one from Google NetPAC, between November 2025 and August 2026. Nothing in the data shows what those contributions were for, and no conclusion about influence follows from them.

The record does not cover committee assignments, floor statements, or anything Scholten said about AI. It also does not show outcomes: every bill entry is a latest status date, and the data does not say whether any bill passed. Three recorded votes appear, and she was absent for all three, which the data reports without explanation.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Hillary Scholten: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 23 events.
